title: Pin the LocalDayClock in epic_27_story_05_bulk_mark_prior_test.dart's second test instead of relying on real wall time

evidence.quote:
// The completion landed "today" (DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() at
      // test execution time) — which is at most a few seconds before

why: No `useLocalDayClock(...)` call exists anywhere in this file, so `repo.markComplete(...)` writes `eventTimestamp` via `DateTimeFactory.nowUtc()` → the real `SystemLocalDayClock`, while `StreakStateProvider(..., clock: FakeLocalDayClock(today))` pins `today = DateTime.utc(2026, 5, 13, 9)` — violating TQ-6's no-wall-clock rule. The in-file comment claiming real 'now' is 'at most a few seconds before `today`' is already false (real time is ~7 weeks past 2026-05-13 as of this audit). The assertion (`state.maxStreak == 1`) only survives because streak_reducer.dart computes maxStreak from distinct-day count, independent of `today`, for a single-event list — confirmed by reading the reducer and by `flutter test` passing today. Any future addition of a currentStreak/lastCompletionDayLocal assertion here would go flaky depending on wall-clock date.
recommendation: Call `useLocalDayClock(FakeLocalDayClock(today))` in setUp with `resetLocalDayClock()` in tearDown, matching the pattern already used in epic_27_integration_lockout_redaction_atomic_test.dart's AC1 group.
acceptance_criteria: Test pins the global LocalDayClock explicitly and passes independent of wall-clock date.
